title: Basie concerts with and without vocalists
summary: Edison and Dance say audiences want to hear Basie's band rather than singers, except with Ella or Sinatra.

story.theme_name: Singers and the musicians who accompanied them

blocks.x: But still -- I mean, I was somewhere -- where was I? Oh, I think it was in Florida or somewhere and he came there and played a two-hour concert with no vocalists and it was very well received.

Oh, everybody wonders why he carries a vocalist, because they don't come to hear Basie introduce a singer and take up that time, where they could be enjoying his music. I don't know why Willard keeps the singer that he's got with him. I don't know why Basie keeps a singer, because he's -- if it's the singer, yeah. But he just occupies some time out there, 15 minutes of time, that the band could be playing, and people want to hear Basie play. They --
Especially when, you know, right now, it's really a bad scene. You know, I mean --
Yeah, they want to hear Basie's band. They don't want to hear somebody sing, not unless he's on a concert tour with Ella. Then he does his 30 minutes and then
Ella will do her -- now that makes a good -- they are a good combination, Ella and Basie. Frank Sinatra and Basie is a good combination. Oh, Frank loves to sing with Basie's band.

But you see, there was one thing I noticed in Florida, now you've got all those elderly people, retired people, they come. You know, that's what that audience was. I mean, the average age must have been 50.
They don't want any rock and roll.
No, they don't want to hear no singing.
They want to hear some music.
